plan.narrative: I'll finish my master's and look for a full-time job elsewhere — the simulator already moves me to full-time once I graduate, so a separate step adds nothing. I keep spending lean and only invest cash above a nine-month cushion, because my emergency fund is cash and I won't sell investments in a dip. My partner and I move in together and look for something bigger once we both earn properly. If cash gets thin I cut spending again rather than move to a cheaper place or borrow — and while I'm still studying I accept that cash may dip, because my income jumps once I graduate.

steps.head: housing
steps.why: We want to live together and more space is worth paying for, but only once two incomes pass the landlord's rule.

steps.head: spending
steps.why: Without a salary my cash would run down fast, and I'd rather cut spending than sell investments.

notes: Dropped the go_full_time step: it was blocked in 13% of lives and the simulator already moves me to full-time once I graduate, so the step added nothing.
Dropped the cheaper_if_short step: it was blocked in 85% of lives because a shared flat is already the cheapest home allowed; instead I protect cash by cutting spending.
Raised the investing buffer from 6 to 9 months of outgoings, because cash fell past the credit limit in half of lives, mostly in 2026 while I was still studying.
Added a second spending cut triggered by low cash, since the job-loss cut alone left 85% of lives dipping below zero.
No sell_to_buffer step: I said I'd cut spending rather than touch investments, so that stays a rule, not an action.
I stay in Zurich — the simulator can't move cities, and I don't want to.
Retirement at 65 is out of reach in this window, so no pension step.
